reasons: **This plan gets the most work done, but cuts it close on heat.** About a third of the important work gets finished. The crew's body heat is expected to come within a hair of the safe limit, so there's almost no room for error. If the day runs hotter than forecast or someone pushes too hard, people could cross into unsafe territory.
**Priya is new and her body isn't used to working in this heat yet.** She shouldn't do any of the hardest physical jobs during the hottest parts of the day, no matter what the schedule pressure is.

**The safer option does less than half the work but leaves a comfortable heat buffer.** It finishes about 14% of the important work instead of 32%, and it keeps Priya on light electrical tasks. Everyone stays well below the heat limit. Choose this plan if the forecast is uncertain or you can't closely watch the crew. Choose the main plan only if you can enforce breaks, water, and shade without exception.

Hard safety rules:
- Every worker's 90th percentile core temperature must stay below 38.0 °C all shift. Harder work, sun and high WBGT heat people up; 30-min shade rests cool them down.
- Breaks: at most 3 work slots in a row, then a 'rest' slot; at most 2 in a row if any of those slots has WBGT >= 30.0 °C.
- No outdoor tasks during hazards that stop outdoor work. After lightning, outdoor work stays stopped for 30 more minutes.
- Workers who are not acclimatized never do very_heavy tasks when WBGT >= 28.0 °C.
Validity: one entry per slot per worker; off-site workers rest; skills and allowed slots must match.
